messages.content: You are one member of a parallel architecture inquiry. Return only the contracted JSON. Produce executable mechanisms, APIs, state transitions, and verification rules; do not propose organizational process or prose-only governance.

Evidence: 84 Claude sessions in five days manually performed environment diagnosis, repository archaeology, architecture reconstruction, research synthesis, Lean proof work, refactors, tests, memory/skill creation, and repeated failure analysis. A transcript audit counted 2,067 direct mutations versus 190 subagent dispatches and about 30% human corrections. Prior harness research specifies carrier adapters with zero substrate intelligence, append-only prompt/tool/result capture, projected memory/context, deterministic tools, governed consolidation only after results, session heartbeats, work claim/settle, and context-compaction continuity. The existing free-compute-dev seed has deterministic resolver -> context -> model edit -> apply -> test -> feedback rounds -> expensive escalation, but only one task and no autonomous intake/decomposition/fanout/tool navigation/isolation/integration/memory. The existing LISS cheapest-sufficient fabric just demonstrated 24/24 schema-verified jobs at 24.45 useful jobs/min across Gemini and GitHub Models, with OpenRouter fallback and Claude available. Future volunteer CPU/GPU endpoints can join over Tailscale. The target is a Union-owned software-production fabric that receives territories/problems and keeps observing, decomposing, executing, verifying, integrating, and learning without a Codex or Claude conversation carrying the work.

Your bounded question: Identify the minimum combined capability set needed to meet or beat Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Paperclip, and Honcho as an autonomous software-production fabric rather than a chatbot.

State what is absent from the current seed, give a concrete design, and name a smallest real vertical slice.

structured_output.absentMechanism: The seed runs one task per session with no durable work queue, no decomposer emitting a dependency DAG, no claim/settle fanout across concurrent workers, no integration oracle merging parallel results, and no memory projector writing patterns between sessions. The 84-session audit (2,067 direct mutations, 30% human corrections) proves work lives in conversation turns, not a fabric. Hermes, OpenClaw, Paperclip, and Honcho each provide at least one of: durable task state, autonomous decomposition, parallel execution isolation, or cross-session context accumulation. The seed provides none of the four.
design: Durable work queue (append-only rows, status: open|claimed|settled|failed): problems land as schema-validated rows; workers poll, heartbeat on TTL, and settle with a result pointer; zero substrate intelligence in the queue itself — it is a log, not a reasoner.

Decomposer agent: accepts a territory spec, emits a JSON DAG of 2–8 subtasks with explicit input/output contracts and dependency edges; result stored durably so identical problems never re-derive their DAG.

Worker executor: for each DAG leaf, spawns an isolated carrier session on the existing LISS fabric, appends every tool call + result to a per-task append-only log, settles when schema-verified output is produced or escalates after N failures — one subtask per session.

Integration oracle: topological walk of the DAG; for each node whose dependencies are settled, runs merge + verification (schema, test suite, static analysis) before promoting status; conflicts on shared output namespaces block promotion.

Memory projector: after full settlement with zero human corrections, extracts (context, action, outcome) triples from append-only logs and writes to a vector store; future decomposer and worker sessions query this store before first tool call.

Escalation router: each subtask carries a token budget; cheap models (Gemini, GitHub Models) dispatch first; persistent failure triggers OpenRouter → Claude escalation; budget consumed is a settled-row field.
Heartbeat monitor: claimed task not heartbeating within TTL is automatically returned to open status; prevents silent API timeouts from masking as in-progress work.
firstVerticalSlice: Write a decomposer that accepts a natural-language software problem and emits a valid JSON DAG of exactly 2–3 subtasks with input/output schemas; gate emission on the existing LISS schema validator.
Insert DAG leaves as rows in the existing LISS job queue — no new queue infrastructure, reuse the proven 24.45 jobs/min substrate.
Execute the two leaf subtasks in parallel on the existing multi-model fabric (Gemini + GitHub Models); each worker appends its tool log to a per-task file.
Implement a linear integrator: concatenate settled outputs in topological order and run schema verification; no branching DAG support in this slice.

On full settlement, write one (problem_statement, dag_json, settled_output_hash) record to a flat JSON memory file; decomposer reads it on the next identical problem and reuses the prior DAG without re-deriving.
failureModes: Decomposer emits subtasks with underspecified input/output contracts → worker cannot begin; mitigation: schema-validate the DAG before any subtask is claimed, re-prompt up to 3 times before escalating.

Parallel workers produce conflicting edits to the same output namespace → integration oracle halts; mitigation: DAG schema enforces disjoint output paths at decomposition time, not at integration time.

Memory projector ingests triples from failed or human-corrected sessions → future lookups steer toward bad patterns; mitigation: project only from sessions where settled_status is verified and human_corrections equals zero.
Claimed task stops heartbeating due to API timeout → appears in-progress but makes no progress; mitigation: TTL monitor returns the row to open within one TTL window, logged as a retry event.

Cost runaway: cheap-model failures cascade into Claude escalations across a large DAG → per-problem budget exhausted mid-graph; mitigation: escalation router checks remaining problem budget before each escalation and fails the subtask rather than exceeding the cap.
structured_output.successMetric: Fabric accepts a 3-part problem (spec, codebase pointer, acceptance tests), decomposes without human input, executes in parallel using cheap models for ≥80% of token spend, verifies against acceptance tests, and completes 5 consecutive problems with zero human corrections at throughput matching the 24.45 jobs/min LISS baseline.
